name: Firebase Studio

status.note: Google announced on 19 March 2026 that it will shut Firebase Studio down on 22 March 2027 and delete remaining data; new workspaces and sign-ups stopped on 22 June 2026.

summary: Google’s browser-based workspace that pairs a Gemini app-prototyping agent with a full Code OSS IDE on a Nix-configured cloud VM; it is being shut down on 22 March 2027 in favor of Google AI Studio and Antigravity.
intro: Firebase Studio gives each workspace a full virtual machine on Google Cloud with a Code OSS editor (the open-source base of VS Code), a terminal, emulators and web and Android previews in the browser. The environment is declared with Nix, covering system packages, language tooling and previews, so a template can carry its whole setup. On top sits the App Prototyping agent: from a prompt, image or drawing it generates a Next.js web app, wires up Genkit with a Gemini API key, and adds Cloud Firestore and Firebase Authentication when the app needs a database or sign-in. You can switch between the agent and the code at any time, and **Publish** deploys to Firebase App Hosting.

It never left preview, so it had no SLA or deprecation policy. On 19 March 2026 Google announced it is folding the product into two others: Google AI Studio for prompt-based prototyping in the browser, and Antigravity, Google’s agent-first desktop IDE, for code-first work. New workspace creation and sign-ups were turned off on 22 June 2026. Existing workspaces keep working until 22 March 2027, when Firebase Studio shuts down and remaining data is deleted for good. A **Move now** button transfers a workspace to AI Studio. Apps already deployed to Firebase, and services such as Firestore, Authentication and App Hosting, are not affected.
strengths: A real Linux VM per workspace, customizable with Nix, so it can run backends, Android emulators and languages beyond JavaScript
The agent sets up Firebase services itself: Firestore, Authentication, a Gemini key for Genkit flows, and App Hosting for publishing
Migration paths are documented: one-click transfer to Google AI Studio, or export to Antigravity, while deployed apps keep running
limits: Being shut down: no new workspaces since 22 June 2026, and all remaining data deleted on 22 March 2027
Always a preview product, with no SLA and no deprecation policy
When moving to AI Studio, the Gemini API key in the workspace’s `.env` file has to be set again by hand as an App Hosting environment variable to keep publishing to the same URL

story: On 8 August 2023 a small Google team shared an experiment called Project IDX: a browser-based development environment built on Google Cloud and Code OSS, where every workspace had the full capabilities of a Linux VM, with templates for Angular, Flutter, Next.js, React, Svelte and Vue, AI help from the Codey model, and deployment to Firebase Hosting. The team’s complaint was that shipping a multiplatform app felt like building a Rube Goldberg machine of tools.

On 9 April 2025, at Cloud Next, Google launched Firebase Studio in preview. It fused Project IDX, Genkit and Gemini in Firebase into one agentic environment and added the App Prototyping agent, which turns a prompt or a drawing into a working Next.js app. Everything from IDX carried over: the Nix-configured VM, emulators, more than 60 templates and imports from GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket. It started with 3 free workspaces, 10 for Google Developer Program members and 30 for premium members.

Less than a year later Google decided to simplify its AI developer tools. On 19 March 2026 it announced the sunset: browser prototyping, with Firestore and Authentication built in, moved to Google AI Studio, and agentic coding to Antigravity. Sign-ups stopped on 22 June 2026, and the service shuts down on 22 March 2027.

choices.choice: A full cloud VM instead of an in-browser sandbox
choices.why: Project IDX wanted development from any device with the full fidelity of local development, so each workspace is a Linux VM hosted in a nearby data center.
Declaring packages, tooling and previews in Nix lets a project share its entire development environment as a template, for a team or the community.

choices.choice: Fold it into AI Studio and Antigravity
choices.why: Google said it was streamlining its tools based on feedback: one browser path from prompt to production, and one agent-first IDE for code-first work, instead of a third product in between.

timeline.text: Project IDX announced on 8 August as an experiment
Firebase Studio launches in preview on 9 April, absorbing Project IDX
Sunset announced on 19 March; migration tools roll out
New workspaces and sign-ups disabled on 22 June
Shutdown and data deletion scheduled for 22 March
